correctness.rationale: For fixed gamma>0 the normalized positive kernel has exact eigenvalues a_m b_n with squared Weyl K-type dimensions. The complete analytic proof derives the exact counting expression, applies a uniform O(1) cutoff inversion for the cubic denominator, controls total rounding errors by O(x^2) using sum h_n^2<infinity, and evaluates the sole harmonic divergence n h_n^2~(A B)^(2/3)/n. The resulting coefficients C=A(gamma+2)/6 and L=(A B)^(2/3)/6, and O(tau^(-2/3)) remainder, follow with no infinite extrapolation from finite experiments. A standalone rational counting checker executed 24 exact diagnostics, supporting arithmetic only.

originality.rationale: Exact K-type eigenvalues and the Schatten criterion are known (Ding 2020). The new assertion is the sharp ordered counting expansion through the universal logarithmic correction at scale tau^(-2/3)log(1/tau), for the full positive critical weight line. It needs uniform two-index cutoff control, summable remainders and extraction of a harmonic divergence; the prior ideal criterion and eigenvalue listing do not themselves establish this ordered two-term asymptotic. Related Dixmier trace results concern rank-one balls or distinct Toeplitz commutators. No decisive duplicate was found in actual semantic and literature checks; the residual unindexed-priority risk is explicit.

value.rationale: The natural critical-weight determinant-kernel family on Cartan I_{2,2} has known ideal membership but an unquantified ordered spectral boundary. The new second Weyl term is a nonvanishing, structurally motivated logarithmic correction arising from the interaction of the two partition coordinates; it lies above the unavoidable O(tau^(-2/3)) discretization scale and is therefore a genuine resolvable spectral invariant. Exact coefficients across every fixed gamma>0 and the resulting noncommutative trace quantify the critical spectral mass. This is more than a routine restatement of the published eigenvalue list or a narrowly selected numerical constant.
